title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Women’s Rights Programme in Kenya, implemented by ActionAid and two women’s rights networks works with 1300 marginalised women and girls, including survivors of violence, who are geographically isolated and economically poor in Taita Taveta and Garissa Counties to create a safer and more just society. The programme specifically aims to a) reduce the risks of gender based violence by increasing the knowledge and skills of marginalised women and girls to advocate for their rights, demand access to GBV services and hold perpetrators to account, b) improve the incomes and sustainability of livelihoods of marginalised women and survivors of violence by enhancing their access to credit and loans, financial business skills, access to markets and leadership in decision making at all levels c) strengthening the resilience of marginalised women and girls to adapt to climate change impacts by increasing their knowledge of adaptation practices to cope with the impacts of climate change and mobilising women, youth and their communities to demand progressive climate policies and budgets that support women and girls. The programme also works with 400 men and boys and 200 local leaders and government officials and 20 institutions to take action in support of women’s rights and demand accountability for violence and discrimination. . OUTCOME: Outcome 3. Marginalized women and survivors of GBV have resilient livelihoods from the impact of climate change and are benefitting from increased funding for climate adaptation initiatives.. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: Objective applies prinicipally to climate action and gender equality. It contributes specifically to adaptation through advocacy and budget participation where partners raised demands on greater budget allocation for climate adapation initiatives and holding government to account for their commitments.
